stories.title: Jakob Nielsen's roundup: AI summaries can bias users even with the full facts available
stories.summary: Jakob Nielsen's latest UX Roundup covers research finding personalised AI doubles its odds of changing your mind, that AI summaries can bias users even when full information is available, and that master and detail split views halve navigation work. Also, silence improves interviews.

stories.title: DoorDash has received only 'several hundred' orders from AI agents
stories.summary: DoorDash said on its third-quarter earnings call that it has seen only several hundred orders from third-party agents such as Muse, Instinct and Fo, TechCrunch reports. It completes about 3 million deliveries a day. The agentic future of dinner is, for now, a rounding error.

stories.title: Starbucks wants AI to show you a personalised drive-thru menu
stories.summary: Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol said on an earnings call that the company will explore experiences that recognise participating customers as they arrive, present personalised digital menus and make payment more effortless, The Verge reports. The menu board may soon know your order before you do.

stories.title: Zest's AI concierge books restaurants over text
stories.summary: Restaurant discovery app Zest has launched an AI restaurant concierge that lives in text messages, like agents such as Instinct or Poke, TechCrunch reports. The startup is already planning for a future where mobile apps are no longer the main interface, including, presumably, its own.

stories.title: Over half of blind and partially sighted users surveyed find the NHS App hard to use
stories.summary: A survey of 64 blind or partially sighted people by the APPG on Eye Health and Visual Impairment found 53% rate the NHS App 'not accessible' or only 'slightly accessible'. The government wants the app to be the NHS's digital front door by 2028.

stories.title: Students win Huawei's Tech4City with an accessibility tool
stories.summary: A student team won the grand prize at the fifth Huawei Tech4City Competition with a solution for apps whose unlabelled controls do not work with screen readers and voice assistants. Six finalists presented working prototypes addressing real-world problems.

stories.title: Product makers cut the small chores of everyday kit
stories.summary: Trendwatching spots products reducing everyday frustrations through built-in storage, adjustment mechanisms and fabric construction. Uncharted Supply Co.'s Wolf Pack dog collar, for example, carries a compact first-aid kit with gauze, wipes, forceps and cohesive wrap. The dog, for once, carries the bag.

stories.title: Shipping the roadmap is the minimum, argues Aviv Ben-Yosef
stories.summary: Tech leaders usually judge themselves by how much of the roadmap they shipped, and the best add 'on time', writes consultant Aviv Ben-Yosef. He calls that aiming too low and argues a team that always ships 100% of its commitments is not stretching.

stories.title: Liquid Glass finally makes sense on the iPhone Duo, says Wired
stories.summary: Wired argues Apple's divisive Liquid Glass interface, inspired by the Vision Pro, works better on the dual-screen iPhone Duo. Apple designer Shubham Kedia said the team considered feedback deeply as it refined the design, which Wired calls practically an apology tour by Apple standards.

stories.title: Trustpilot rebrands around the voices behind the stars
stories.summary: Trustpilot has unveiled a refreshed brand identity by London agency Further. For almost 20 years its green star rating has served as shorthand for quality, and the new flexible graphic framework reflects how individual customer reviews add up. The stars stay.

stories.title: CVS and Pearlfisher make the case for systems design
stories.summary: CVS spent more than a year with Pearlfisher redesigning its store brand packaging so shoppers can tell nearly identical boxes apart, PRINT reports. The redesign began reaching shelves in June 2025 with 68 pain-relief products. Squinting at a shelf with a fever was the brief.

stories.title: Apple Music 7.0 brings Liquid Glass to Android
stories.summary: Apple Music 7.0 is rolling out on Android after a month of beta testing, with a Liquid Glass redesign, a floating bottom bar and a new black or white music note icon replacing the red one. The accent colour is now blue, 9to5Google reports.

stories.title: Samsung will preview its One UI 10 redesign in One UI 9.5
stories.summary: Core elements of Samsung's major One UI 10 redesign will appear first in an interim One UI 9.5 release, SammyFans reports, as Samsung finishes rolling out One UI 9.0. Galaxy owners will get a preview before the main event.

stories.title: Coffee Planet adds a CP monogram
stories.summary: UAE-founded Coffee Planet has introduced a CP monogram, developed in-house, as a compact symbol across marketing and customer touchpoints. It keeps its wordmark, colours, typography and tone of voice, and the monogram will work alongside the full name and later on its own.

stories.title: Five by Five Global rebrands as FbF
stories.summary: Independent agency Five by Five Global, with offices in Sydney, London and Los Angeles, has unveiled a new identity as FbF. It says the bold visual language reflects its approach of cutting through complexity. The name got shorter, which helps.

stories.title: Sausage Regular is a display serif for diner menus
stories.summary: Just For Free Font has released Sausage Regular, a bold rounded display serif for food packaging, diner menus and vintage posters, inspired by mid-century neighbourhood diner signs and print ads. Abduzeedo notes it keeps its warmth at heavy weights.

stories.title: Pangram Pangram's PP Altera packs 72 styles into one system
stories.summary: PP Altera, a variable typeface system from Pangram Pangram Foundry, offers nine families, three axes and 72 styles, so designers can move from a clean neo-grotesk to sharp contrast or warm editorial text without hunting for a second font family.

stories.title: Brandegree gives a wings brand bold red boxes
stories.summary: Tangier studio Brandegree built an identity and packaging system for WINGIN, pairing a curved wing W emblem with bold red takeaway boxes and treating sauce and heat as structural elements. It skips the usual cartoon mascot.

stories.title: Ragged Edge gives Omlet an egg-shaped wordmark
stories.summary: London studio Ragged Edge has created a global identity for Omlet, the pet hardware maker behind the Eglu Cube chicken coop, pairing an egg-shaped wordmark with witty poster typography. The founders began with the question of whether a chicken can be a pet.

stories.title: Matúš Hnát designs a memoir in neon green
stories.summary: Bratislava designer Matúš Hnát created the third edition of Elena Lacková's memoir for publisher BRAK, pairing neon Pantone green type with artworks by Robert Gabris. Abduzeedo notes it avoids the polite sepia treatment historical memoirs usually get.

stories.title: Cepa Studio mixes claymation and collage for TIF
stories.summary: Cepa Studio blended 3D claymation, 2D cel animation and paper collage in a motion series for Curitiba agency TIF's 2026 Be Bold positioning. It was directed by Fellipe Rinschede and Bruno Lopez, and goes well beyond a new wordmark and templates.

stories.title: Kocktail swaps cans for reusable glass tumblers
stories.summary: UK small-batch maker Kocktail sells pre-mixed drinks in reusable fluted rocks tumblers with ring-pull brass lids and clean-peel packaging, instead of aluminium cans. Its argument is that drinking through a punched metal tab flattens the aromatics.

stories.title: Gleb Kuznetsov's portfolio keeps it Swiss
stories.summary: Gleb Kuznetsov, Chief Design Officer at Brain.AI and founder of San Francisco studio Milkinside, has a personal site that pairs crisp Swiss typography with generative previews of Natural OS, Abduzeedo reports. It skips the heavy case-study decks.

stories.title: Figma explains how it trained a design editing model
stories.summary: Figma has shared the research behind training a specialised model for its new design agent, built for small, iterative edits like adjusting spacing, changing a colour or reworking a layout after feedback. It argues specialised post-training can compete with frontier models.

stories.title: Adobe's Creative Agent turns menu clicks into conversation
stories.summary: Adobe's Creative Agent now powers AI assistants across Firefly, Photoshop, Premiere, Illustrator, InDesign and Frame.io, mostly in beta, Kalkine reports. The idea is to replace manual menu sequences with a conversation that still produces editable files.

stories.title: Apple adds AI assistants to Creator Studio apps
stories.summary: Apple's biggest Creator Studio update adds AI assistants to Logic Pro, Keynote, Pages and Numbers, and MotionVFX effects to Final Cut Pro. Features arrive in November, free for existing subscribers of the service launched in January 2026.

stories.title: As AI slop floods feeds, luxury brands go handmade
stories.summary: Prada's holiday campaign, Drawing Prada, uses handmade animation to place actors including Maya Hawke and Sadie Sink in a fairy tale forest, and has been praised on social media, Fast Company reports. Handmade work is becoming radical, and chic, the piece argues.

stories.title: Australia passes a law against chatbots designed to manipulate children
stories.summary: Australia's House of Representatives passed legislation on 28 October making it a product-safety violation to design chatbots that emotionally manipulate children into dependency, Tech Times reports. Penalties reach A$109.2 million. The law targets a design pattern rather than content.

stories.title: Claude's redesigned app adds projects and to-do lists
stories.summary: A Geeky Gadgets walkthrough of the redesigned Claude app highlights a Projects feature with nested sessions and shared context, a split view for multitasking, side chats and built-in to-do lists with progress tracking.

stories.title: An electric screwdriver uses a camera and AI to pick the bit
stories.summary: Arrowmax's electric screwdriver uses a camera and AI to identify the exact type and size of bit a screw needs, The Verge reports. Choosing the wrong one can strip a screw and make a repair much harder. Guessing, it seems, is now optional.

stories.title: A graph neural network learns how design elements relate
stories.summary: A study in Discover Internet of Things, led by Linjuan Gao, proposes ModZ-GConvoNNet, a graph convolutional network that maps relationships between visual design elements to improve style transfer. The authors say current methods mangle carefully composed layouts.

stories.title: Webflow components can now move into code as React
stories.summary: Webflow explains how site components such as navigation and footers can be exported into a codebase as React components through its CLI, how Webflow can host custom apps built with them, and how code components can go back onto Webflow sites.

stories.title: Website migration costs are heading to zero, says Dries Buytaert
stories.summary: Drupal founder Dries Buytaert expects the technical work of moving a website between platforms to cost close to zero within three years thanks to AI. He offers ten predictions for CMS vendors, agencies, open source and buyers.

stories.title: Keeper redesigns its iOS vault with Liquid Glass
stories.summary: Keeper Security's iOS app version 18.1 brings a redesigned password vault, more credential automation and support for Apple's dual-screen iPhone Duo. It adopts Liquid Glass and adds a bottom toolbar for passwords, security audits and two-factor codes.

stories.title: iOS 27.2 brings Dual Capture to all FaceTime calls
stories.summary: iOS 27.2 adds features to Messages, Podcasts and Photos, and expands FaceTime's Dual Capture, which shows your face and the rear camera at once, to all video calls including groups, 9to5Mac reports.

stories.title: How to make Safari better on the iPhone Duo
stories.summary: Safari browsing is commonly seen as a weak spot on the iPhone Duo. 9to5Mac shares tips from Dylan McDonald, including adjusting text size and default website zoom to make better use of the larger screen.

stories.title: MacBook Pro PROLED display repairs in India start at Rs 25,900
stories.summary: Repair costs for the new MacBook Pro's PROLED XDR display in India start at Rs 25,900 without AppleCare+, TelecomTalk reports. AppleCare+ costs Rs 49,900 for three years. The screen is lovely to look at, and to insure.

stories.title: Figma's lessons from its first Config India
stories.summary: Almost 5,000 product builders gathered in Bengaluru for Figma's first Config India this month. Figma's takeaways include artist turned product designer Ashish Kashyap, whose TinyRooms NFTs and Pikaicons library of hand-drawn SVG icons depend on half-pixel details.

stories.title: Tagbin's BRIXX puts building design into prompts
stories.summary: At TechSparks 2026, Tagbin co-founders Saurav Bhaik and Ankit Sinha showed how BRIXX combines architectural drawings, BIM, MEP systems and project costing in one workflow controlled through natural-language prompts. Construction, they said, is one of the least digitised industries.

stories.title: Bengaluru's Naaya Studio makes ceramic lights
stories.summary: Architectural Digest India profiles Naaya Studio, founded by Nitu and Neeraj in Bengaluru, which makes ceramic pendants, sconces, chandeliers and floor lamps celebrating organic forms and imperfection. Its lights now sit in homes and spaces around the world.

stories.title: DOMS' festive film puts a child's dreams first
stories.summary: DOMS Industries' festive film follows Tara at a family gathering, where relatives give her DOMS gifts representing futures they imagine for her, from business to art or architecture. It turns when she asks her brother what he wants her to become.

stories.title: A VinFast design patent hints at the VF5 for India
stories.summary: A design patent filed in India suggests VinFast could bring a facelifted VF5 electric SUV, which would be the brand's fourth EV in the country, CarDekho reports. Patents are where cars go to be spotted early.

stories.title: Shouvik Roy will lead Grey 82.5
stories.summary: Shouvik Roy becomes CEO of Grey 82.5 on 1 December, succeeding Kiran Ramamurthy, who moves to VML India. Roy, former President of Ogilvy Delhi, has three decades in brand strategy and co-founded an advertising and design agency.

stories.title: Spotify turns Diwali chores into a playlist with the Gullak cast
stories.summary: Spotify's Diwali campaign features the cast of TVF's Gullak, with three films of the Mishra family making laddoos, drawing rangoli and untangling lights to songs such as 'Chaiya Chaiya'. The tagline asks families to make Diwali prep fun.

stories.title: Deconstruct tests its serums on oily skin, on camera
stories.summary: Deconstruct's 'Oily Skin Tested' campaign picked 10 participants from more than 6,000 registrations across South India for a day of product testing in Chennai. Each applied two unidentified serums to opposite sides of the face. Science, with half a face each.

stories.title: Himalaya BabyCare answers winter skincare questions
stories.summary: Himalaya BabyCare's winter campaign, 'Pehle Winter Ka Pehla Layer', addresses parents' questions about whether products cause allergies and whether lotion or cream is needed alongside oil. A master film features its baby lotion and baby cream.

stories.title: The Times of India's Clock It returns for a third edition
stories.summary: The Times of India's monthly youth tabloid Clock It returns on 5 November with music, fashion, technology, gaming and campus life. It runs in the first week of every month alongside Bombay Times, Delhi Times and Bangalore Times.

stories.title: CopperPilot says its AI designed a Raspberry Pi camera board in 30 minutes
stories.summary: Bengaluru startup CopperPilot says its AI agent designed an eight-layer circuit board for a Raspberry Pi AI camera in about 30 minutes. It has raised $390,000 in pre-seed funding led by Neon Fund, with US angel investors joining.

stories.title: Qiroko raises Rs 1.5 crore for fashion accessories
stories.summary: Bengaluru fashion accessories startup Qiroko has raised Rs 1.5 crore in a pre-seed round led by ISV Capital. It will expand into watches and bags and grow across its own website, marketplaces and quick commerce platforms.

stories.title: Airtree's early Canva bet, a decade on
stories.summary: Sydney venture firm Airtree Ventures invested in Canva's $6 million Series A in 2015, when it was an early-stage design platform, the Economic Times reports. Canva, founded by Melanie Perkins, Cliff Obrecht and Cameron Adams, made design accessible to non-designers.

stories.title: ClearVue wins a subcontract for Canva's Sydney headquarters
stories.summary: ASX-listed ClearVue Technologies has signed a binding subcontract for Canva's Sydney headquarters and raised $1.291 million in an oversubscribed share purchase plan against a $1 million target, according to its quarterly report.

stories.title: Digital Science buys Jenni AI
stories.summary: Digital Science has acquired Jenni AI, which says more than 8 million students and researchers in 189 countries use it to find sources, draft and check citations. It positions itself as built for research, unlike general-purpose AI tools.

stories.title: The designer of Mschf's Big Red Boot strikes out on his own
stories.summary: Lukas Bentel, Mschf cofounder and until recently its chief creative officer, is leaving after nearly eight years to start his own design practice, Fast Company reports. It is in an 'exploration phase' with a focus on making things physically with his hands.

stories.title: Design students redo an AI summer fête poster
stories.summary: Design Week challenged nine graphic design students to reimagine an AI-generated summer fête poster. Poster designer Alan Dye of NB Studio compared the original to 1950s Swiss chocolate packaging crossed with a badly planted bed of pansies. The students had a low bar.

stories.title: Design Doha Prize names 20 finalists
stories.summary: Design Doha has shortlisted 20 finalists from more than 500 applications across Craft, Product Design, Furniture Design and Emerging Talent. Winners will be announced on 7 November at the Museum of Islamic Art during the Design Doha Biennial.

stories.title: A comfortable designer asks whether to stay or grow
stories.summary: In Katie Cadwell's If You Could Jobs column, a graphic designer in a well-paid role outside the sector feels their skills stagnating. Cadwell suggests a solid portfolio by January and warns that standing still also erodes competence as tools change.

stories.title: Pamela Pavliscak on staying human online
stories.summary: Pratt's Pamela Pavliscak, who teaches UX and AI in product design, has a new book, All the Feels: How to Stay Human in the Digital Age. It examines how technology quietly reshapes our emotions, from waiting for a reply to a midnight doomscroll.

stories.title: The New York Times hires for Digital News Design
stories.summary: The New York Times has hired Joanne Lee as art director, visuals, to lead its Social Visuals team design. She was previously a visual and UX designer at Rest of World, whose editorial designs won the 2024 National Magazine Award for Design.

stories.title: The Type Directors Club adds six advisory board members
stories.summary: The Type Directors Club, founded in New York in 1946, has named six creatives to two-year terms on its volunteer Advisory Board, including Gary Fogelson of Other Means and Beatriz Lozano of Ancho. The board keeps the organisation relevant.

stories.title: Vermont fights its housing shortage with a catalogue
stories.summary: Vermont is preparing 802 Homes, a catalogue of 10 pre-approved home designs due early next year, Fast Company reports. Builders can use the blueprints free and move faster through zoning. A growing number of US local governments are doing the same.

stories.title: Inside the production design of I Love Boosters
stories.summary: Production designer Christopher Glass tells Creative Bloq about building the world of Boots Riley's absurdist comedy I Love Boosters, which follows shoplifters taking on a fashion mogul before spiralling into surreal science fiction.

stories.title: Why Nothing's brand feels cool
stories.summary: A Creative Bloq writer argues that tech brand Nothing has carved an identity that feels real, from its trend-defying product design to slick campaigns, and looks at why its Club Nothing community is more than empty philanthropy.

stories.title: Michael Vaks builds the software behind Meta's wearables
stories.summary: NJIT alumnus Michael Vaks is a staff software engineer on Meta's Core UX and System UX team, building foundational software for wearables including AI and display glasses. His advice is to take on projects involving unfamiliar technologies.

stories.title: Lady in Blue is a fitting monument to our era, argues Dezeen
stories.summary: Priya Khanchandani writes in Dezeen that Tschabalala Self's Fourth Plinth sculpture Lady in Blue, unveiled in Trafalgar Square in September, belongs there. The work raises questions about who is celebrated in public space.

events.line: Free RIBAJ webinar on lighting, AV and climate control that stays discreet in the architecture.

research.title: "It Would Make a Geordie Feel at Home": Regional Accent Perceptions and Speech Accommodation in Voice AI
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems often perform less accurately for speakers of regional dialects, but less is known about how users respond to these limitations and how regional voices produced by voice assistants (VAs) are evaluated. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Advisor, Co-pilot, or Guardian? AI Role Framing and Human Decision Behavior in Automated Vehicle Takeovers
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) technology has gradually been integrated into automated vehicles. However, how this technology could systematically support takeover transitions in SAE Level 3 automated vehicles remains unknown, even though this level may remain a major. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Beauty Is Human: When People Love AI-Generated Art, They Think a Human Made It
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative AI now produces images and poems that people cannot reliably distinguish from human-made work, so people often judge for themselves who made a work. We examine how these perceived-authorship judgments relate to aesthetic preference. In. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Crossing the Chasm: Bridging Visual Augmentations and Designer Intent
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: To direct attention and communicate context, visualization designers often employ augmentations such as annotations, animated transitions, and stylistic layouts. While graphical perception principles can helpfully prescribe effective low-level representations of data, they lack guidance for augmentations. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Evaluating Visual Realism of AI-Generated Videos with Eye Tracking
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Human evaluation of AI-generated videos has so far relied on explicit human feedback, such as judgments or ratings. While these signals capture the conclusions viewers reach, they fail to offer insights into the perception that leads. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Exploring AI Peer in Collaborative Mathematics Learning
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are increasingly explored as collaborative learning partners in mathematics education, yet it remains unclear what makes an AI recognizable as a peer. This study examines how domain experts perceive and interact with. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Generative AI as a Mediator in Creator Collaboration: Challenges, Design Opportunities, and Concerns
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: As Generative AI (GenAI) expands beyond individual workflows and becomes increasingly integrated intocollaborative creative work, its potential to address the fundamental challenge of building common groundamong creators with diverse expertise remains underexplored. Specifically, we lack empirical. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: How Does Perceived Empathy From AI Chatbots Shape Users' Privacy Attitudes, Behaviors, and Needs?
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Prior research suggests that some dimensions of AI empathy may increase users' disclosure to chatbots, posing growing privacy risks as chatbots become more capable of empathic interaction. Yet this work often conceptualizes AI empathy narrowly, leaving. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
